A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CorrGCV research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and Appendices A–K support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V5 reports original synthetic regression experiments, empirical bias–variance decompositions and numerical spectral checks in the main figures and appendices.

after.justification: V6 retains these original regression simulations, bias–variance results and numerical checks.

M1.justification: The central CorrGCV estimator and computational workflow remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 corrects the auxiliary recipe for estimating the sample S-transform from the empirical Gram matrix by requiring deconvolution of feature covariance, and distinguishes this from using a direct estimate of sample correlations.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian regression scenarios: isotropic and anisotropic features, exponential/nearest-neighbor/power-law correlations, matched and mismatched noise, and correlated test points.

E2.justification: Ordinary GCV/Naive GCV1, Altman's correction/Naive GCV2 and Carmack's estimator remain in their corresponding comparisons, including Appendix G. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The corresponding figures retain their dimensions, ridge parameters, noise levels, correlation settings and risk measures. V6 newly clarifies that the power-law experiments used known population correlations; v5 Appendix J already described inversion of the population degrees-of-freedom function, so this does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The double-descent, noise-mismatch, forecast-horizon, bias–variance, spectral and duality analyses are retained. Appendix E expands mathematical justification without adding a new empirical or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both Appendix K versions specify error bars over ten different datasets and the same ensemble procedure. No repeated-run counts or uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: The corresponding plotted results and reported empirical findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. V5 Figures 7–19 correspond to v6 Figures 8–20; their renumbering follows conversion of the code listing into Figure 7.

T1.justification: V6 repairs normalization and resolvent arguments in Lemma III.4, the training-risk exponent in Theorem IV.2, derivative and risk identities in Appendix C, MMSE normalization in H, and both explicit S-transform formulas in I. Appendix E also corrects source/risk scaling expressions and replaces its brief smooth-symbol argument with an integral, Abel-regularization and uniform eigenvalue-bound proof. These substantially revise mathematical correctness and justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about correlated-sample risk asymptotics, CorrGCV's asymptotic exactness under matched correlations, mismatch duality and optimism from temporally nearby test points.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly explains that the empirical Gram matrix mixes sample and feature correlations. It qualifies recovery of the sample S-transform by requiring feature-covariance information or isotropic features, narrowing the applicability of v5's unqualified estimation recipe.

D1.justification: The Appendix A code fixes undefined identifiers and replaces an incorrect derivative product with the ratio required by the retained main-text algorithm. V6 also explicitly documents known population correlations in the power-law experiments. Hardware, compute usage and repository access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix I.1 newly identifies its Toeplitz spectral calculation as a special case of general limit results, citing the already-referenced Böttcher et al. work. This is a limited positioning refinement; the cited-work set and principal comparisons with earlier research remain stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the scientific section sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites in Appendices A and E, typo and cross-reference corrections, an explicit Introduction heading, removal of the generic Impact statement, and relocation of references after the appendices.

P2.justification: V6 replaces the two-column main-text format with a single-column layout, substantially changing equation displays, typography and figure placement. Figures 3 and 6 change from stacked to side-by-side panels, and the expanded code listing becomes Figure 7. The plotted evidence itself is retained.

improvement.justification: V6 substantially improves mathematical reliability and reproducibility: it repairs central identities and explicit S-transforms, corrects the faulty implementation listing, qualifies the invalid general Gram-matrix estimation recipe, and supplies a stronger proof supporting the scaling result. These resolve important deficiencies in a primarily theoretical paper. The benefits arise from correctness and usable documentation, while the empirical evidence and central claims remain unchanged.
